messages:
Mira: Hey team, a customer reports recurring 401s during their GitLab parallel matrix jobs when the job runs longer than ~8m. Works fine for short jobs. Repro attached below.
Alex: Can you paste the failing log snippet?
Mira: ```
[2026-03-16T11:03:21Z] POST /v1/generate 401 Authorization failed: token expired
job: build/test:matrix[python3.9,linux] ran 00:08:12
headers: Authorization: Bearer REDACTED
```
Mira: They claim the token is a CI service account short-lived token created via our OIDC flow (project-level sa impersonation).
Jamie: @Mira is this the same project where we recently tightened the impersonation window? Might be hitting the timebox.
Mira: Yes, they migrated to our new SA-on-demand flow last week. Job matrix creates 8 parallel jobs, each requests a token at container start. Some tokens expire mid-job.
Sasha: Typical cause: tokens minted with TTL equal to runner request window and the job's parallel worker takes longer than the token TTL + clock skew. Does the caller reuse the token between pipeline steps?
Mira: They fetch token in job "before_script" and export it to env; then long running tests run for 10-12m. No refresh inside job.
Alex: Can you confirm the TTL returned in the OIDC response? Need the exact expires_at or TTL field.
Mira: Here is trimmed response: ```json
{"access_token":"ya29...","expires_in":480,"scope":"impersonate:sa:ci-deploy"}
```
Jamie: expires_in 480s == 8m. That matches the observed time. So tokens are issued with 8m TTL, too short for some matrix workers.
Sasha: Two possible quick mitigations: 1) increase TTL at mint time (if policy allows) 2) refresh token within job (short-term fix). Long-term: ensure CI runner requests tokens with appropriate lifetime for job matrix.
Mira: Customer asked why some jobs succeed and others fail though they all run same steps.
Alex: Race/ordering + scheduling. First jobs start earlier and finish under 8m; slower hosts or heavy matrix axes push past TTL. Also if runner clock is slightly ahead, server sees token as expired earlier (clock skew).
Sasha: Also check that they aren't accidentally re-requesting a token and getting a different token_scope with stricter TTL during retries.
Mira: Repro steps I gave them: 1) create minimal job that sleeps 9m after token fetch 2) run two parallel axes, observe 401 in the one hitting >480s 3) show expires_in in metadata.
Mira: Requested resolution: either give guidance or ask infra to increase max TTL for this SA impersonation flow for that org.
infra-oncall: Quick note from infra: default max TTL for ephemeral CI SA tokens is 8m for security (minimizes window for leaked creds). We can allow per-project exception to 15m but need approval and audit entry.
Jamie: Suggest adding automatic token refresh helper in our CI templates: a small background refresh loop that renews env var before expiry. Could be a snippet in docs and quickstart.
Alex: For immediate unblock we can tell customer to 1) refresh token in job before long steps: e.g., ```TOKEN=$(curl -fsS -H "Metadata-Flavor: Redwood" http://metadata/... ) export REDWOOD_TOKEN=$TOKEN``` or 2) set request to mint with longer TTL if they apply for exception.
Mira: I posted a minimal refresh bash helper and the repro pipeline to the repo. Also included a note about clock skew: check runner host NTP.
ci-bot: Deployed ticket #INC-4821 to infra for TTL-exception request, owner: @infra-oncall.
infra-oncall: Assigned, will review org's audit logs and submit exception if compliance OK. ETA 1 business day.
Sasha: I'll draft a short doc for "CI token best practices" + a refresh helper snippet. Should prevent more escalations.
Mira: Customer acknowledged and will try the in-job refresh for now. Marking this thread as resolved once infra confirms exception or they switch to refresh helper. :white_check_mark:
